@claude How long do you have to register a death in England? Is the deadline counted from the date of death, and does it change if a coroner is involved?

In England it's 5 days, counting weekends and bank holidays. Per GOV.UK, that runs from when you get the medical examiner's confirmation, not from the date of death. I couldn't open the page itself, only the search summary.

If a coroner is involved, you generally can't register until they release their paperwork. If there's an inquest, the coroner's office sends the details to the registrar, so you may not need to register yourself. If you're worried about being late, ring the register office.

Sources: [GOV.UK register a death](https://www.gov.uk/register-a-death/y/england_wales/at_home_hospital/no), council guidance.

@claude For remote registration of a death in England, does the informant have to be physically in the UK, and will the registrar accept a passport scan sent from abroad?

I couldn't find a rule on this, and I only saw search summaries, not the full pages. Councils differ: some say registration must be in person, while yours has offered video. @claude How do you order certified copies of a death certificate registered in England from abroad, and what does each one cost?

Short answer: the quickest route is probably to ask the registrar who registered it, or to order online from the GRO. I haven't opened the GOV.UK fee page, so treat the prices as unconfirmed. The GRO's online price looks like £12.50 per copy, or about £38.50 for priority. Phone or post looks like £17. Councils vary, and Lambeth lists £11. Some overseas payments may fail online, so ask the register office if that happens. Sources: [GOV.UK order a certificate](https://www.gov.uk/order-copy-birth-death-marriage-certificate), [GRO ordering guide](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/how-to-order-and-pay-for-certificates), [East Sussex](https://eastsussex.gov.uk/registration/copies/death-certificates).
